code.note: A shell archive (Algorithm:734, Language Fortran90, Precision Sp). Members: Src/Sp/src.f90 (the minimisation package, modules precisions, reals, supp_codes, minimize and others), Drivers/Sp/driver2.f90 (Rosenbrock test program, Min_Rosenbrock, self-contained: no stdin), Drivers/Sp/res2 (the shipped stdout of that run). driver2 calls i1mach(2) for the output unit, which is not in the archive (PackingList names the PORT library, DriverLib: port); the rerun must supply i1mach, for example a function returning 6 for unit 2. Needs a Fortran 90 compiler; gfortran is not in the scout sandbox.

field: numerics (unconstrained minimisation, quasi-Newton and conjugate gradient in single precision)

claim.location: Shipped reference run Drivers/Sp/res2: the stdout of driver2.f90. Minimise the Rosenbrock function f = 100(x2-x1^2)^2 + (1-x1)^2 from x = (-1.2, 1) with acc = 0.001, Frequency = 10, EvalLimit = 200, state Normal (module RosenbrockFunc in driver2.f90). The printed lines are 'Least function value: 0.20053597E-08.', 'Function evaluation count: 59.', 'Iteration count: 36.'

reference.file: Fortran90/Drivers/Sp/res2 (member of 734.gz shar, between the 'res2' cat marker and its SHAR_EOF)

claim.metric: Function evaluation count, iteration count and least function value printed by driver2.f90 (format e16.8)
claim.paper_value: Shipped res2 only. The paper was not read, so no paper value is used.

tolerance.abs: 0 for both counts; 1e-8 absolute for the least function value
tolerance.why: The counts are integers from the method's path, so they must match exactly. The least value is at single-precision rounding noise near the minimum (about 2e-9), so a tighter absolute tolerance would test rounding, not the method. Scout chose these tolerances after reading the shipped res2 value (the value is not a run of ours); the rerun must not loosen them to fit its own result.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: well under 1 minute (59 function evaluations on a 2-variable problem); the archive's other test programs are larger and are not in scope here
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the archive's ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text it finds in the archive

why: A 1994 Fortran 90 minimiser ships a deterministic driver and its printed run; the iteration and evaluation counts are exact integers from the method, so a rerun checks the algorithm's path, not only its endpoint.
